To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the observing response is the mechanism that mediates the control exerted by stimuli that are correlated with different reinforcement contingencies and that the control exerted in this way is independent of the specific stimulus used to signal reinforcement.
the amount of observing of a stimulus is a direct determinant of its control over behavior.

the observing response is the mechanism by which the stimulus control of behavior is established and maintained, and that the control of the observing response itself is established by the correlation of stimuli with different rates of reinforcement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the environment on the behavior of the organism.
how we learn to respond selectively to the relevant stimuli in our environment, and the observing analysis is our current best guess as to how this process occurs.
the development of a theory of discrimination learning based on the concepts of observing and attention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observing-response hypothesis provides a more complete and satisfactory account of stimulus control than does the response-strengthening hypothesis.
stimulus control is a function of attention, which in turn is a function of observing.
the observing response is a powerful and versatile tool that can account for a wide variety of data and that can be used to generate new predictions and hypotheses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more we know about how organisms respond to their environment, the more we can predict their behavior.
the more a subject observes and attends to the relevant stimuli, the more control those stimuli have over the subject's behavior.
we have found that the behavior of the organism is not the only important determinant of learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
observing and attending to stimuli is a critical component to establishing stimulus control.
observing is a fundamental mechanism in establishing stimulus control and is a critical factor in understanding the effects of reinforcement schedules and other variables.
the observing response is an important factor in establishing stimulus control.
